item.text:
I used the supplied local priors as the baseline and did not re-fetch structured country-year datasets already covered there. The sources below add ruler-specific narrative, constitutional, and event context only, with no scoring.

**Office and constraints**
- Shehbaz Sharif became Prime Minister of Pakistan in April 2022 after Imran Khan was removed in a no-confidence process.
- Constitutionally, the PM is the chief executive and is elected by the National Assembly, but in 2022 Sharif governed through a coalition with a slim parliamentary base.
- The main practical constraints in 2022 were coalition fragility, severe macro stress, the summer flood emergency, rights pressure around protest/repression, and the formal civil-military appointment process.

**Retained sources**
| Family | Source | Direct URL | Precise fact | Fit / attribution | Limits / contrary points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary legal | `Chapter 3: The Federal Government` (Pakistani constitutional text mirror, undated) | https://www.pakistani.org/pakistan/constitution/part3.ch3.html | Executive authority is exercised by the federal government through the PM, who is the chief executive; the National Assembly elects the PM. | Core authority baseline for 2022; formal office, not personal performance. | Legal text does not show informal power centers or how politics works in practice. |
| Independent wire | `Pakistan's prime minister Imran Khan ousted in no-confidence vote in parliament` (Reuters via Investing.com, 2022-04-09) | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/pakistan-parliament-adjourns-to-reconvene-on-vote-to-oust-pm-khan-speaker-2801011 | Khan was removed in a no-confidence vote after coalition partners defected, creating the opening for Sharif. | Directly explains the transition into Sharif's premiership. | Focuses on Khan's ouster, not Sharif's later governing record; opposition treated it as a regime-change plot. |
| Primary official | `PM confident of tackling high inflation, economic challenges` (APP, 2022-04-11) | https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-confident-of-tackling-high-inflation-economic-challenges/ | The article reports that Sharif took the oath of office as PM on April 11, 2022. | Best official source for office assumption on the exact day he took power. | State framing; no opposition critique or implementation follow-up. |
| Primary official | `33-member 'coalition cabinet' takes oath` (APP, 2022-04-19) | https://www.app.com.pk/top-news/34-member-coalition-cabinet-takes-oath/ | A 33-member cabinet from multiple parties was sworn in a week after Sharif took office. | Shows the coalition structure and cabinet breadth that shaped his governing constraints. | Ceremonial event; does not reveal intra-coalition bargaining or policy disputes. |
| Independent wire | `Pakistan consumer price inflation at 14-year high of 24.9% in July` (Reuters via The Economic Times, 2022-08-01) | https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/world-news/pakistan-consumer-price-inflation-at-14-year-high-of-24-9-in-july/articleshow/93274769.cms?from=mdr | Inflation hit 24.9% in July 2022, with fuel, electricity, food, reserves, and currency pressure all worsening. | Strong inherited-condition source for economic stress during Sharif's first months. | It is a macro snapshot, not a ruler-specific causal analysis. |
| Critical NGO | `Pakistan: Protests by families of the disappeared met with intimidation, harassment and violence` (Amnesty International, 2022-08-11) | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2022/08/pakistan-protests-by-families-of-the-disappeared-met-with-intimidation-harassment-and-violence/ | Amnesty says peaceful protest by families of the disappeared was met with intimidation and violence by authorities. | Useful for Chapter 3B and 4B because it captures rights pressure and state response under Sharif's government. | Advocacy framing; focuses on a specific protest subset and not the entire protest landscape. |
| Local-language, favorable | `وزیراعظم نے سیلاب سے متاثرہ افراد کی امداد کیلئے ریلیف فنڈ قائم کر دیا` (Radio Pakistan Urdu, 2022-08-06) | https://urdu.radio.gov.pk/06-08-2022/ozir-aaathm-n-silab-s-mtathr-afrad-ki-amdad-kile-rilif-fn-kaem-kr-dia | Sharif announced a flood relief fund, appealed for donations, and said emergency measures were already being taken. | Best retained Urdu-language source for Sharif's own public framing of flood response. | State broadcaster account; it reflects announcement and intent, not audited delivery or impact. |
| Independent wire | `Facing 'severe' energy crisis, Pakistan reverts to five-day work week` (Reuters via Euronews, 2022-06-08) | https://www.euronews.com/2022/06/08/pakistan-energy | The cabinet approved a five-day workweek to cut energy and fuel use amid severe power shortages. | Good inherited-condition source for the energy squeeze early in Sharif's tenure. | Brief explainer; it does not by itself establish responsibility or implementation quality. |
| Primary/UN | `2022 Pakistan Floods Response Plan - FRP` (United Nations in Pakistan, 2022-09-02) | https://pakistan.un.org/en/197499-2022-pakistan-floods-response-plan-frp | The UN says severe monsoon weather since June caused widespread flooding; by late August 72 districts had been declared calamity-hit. | Strong disaster-context source for Chapters 6B and 8B. | UN synthesis; counts were dynamic and continued to change as the crisis evolved. |
| Primary/international | `Pakistan Flood Damages and Economic Losses Over USD 30 billion and Reconstruction Needs Over USD 16 billion - New Assessment` (World Bank, 2022-10-28) | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/10/28/pakistan-flood-damages-and-economic-losses-over-usd-30-billion-and-reconstruction-needs-over-usd-16-billion-new-assessment | PDNA estimated damages above $14.9bn, losses about $15.2bn, and reconstruction needs at least $16.3bn. | Best retained source for the scale of the flood shock inherited and managed during 2022. | Modeled estimate after the fact; later revisions can shift totals. |
| Primary/international | `Pakistan: Seventh, and Eighth Reviews of the Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility...` (IMF, 2022-09-01) | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2022/09/01/pakistan-seventh-and-eighth-reviews-of-the-extended-arrangement-under-the-extended-fund-522800 | The IMF report says Sharif came to power after the no-confidence vote and that the governing coalition had only a slim majority in a complex political environment. | Best retained source for coalition fragility and macro-policy constraint framing. | IMF lens prioritizes program continuity and macro stability over the full domestic political story. |
| Primary/legal | `President appoints Lt Gen. Sahir Shamshad Mirza as CJCSC and Lt Gen. Asim Munir as COAS` (President of Pakistan, 2022-11-24) | https://president.gov.pk/news/president-appoints-lt-gen-sahir-shamshad-mirza-as-cjcsc-and-lt-gen-asim-munir-as-coas | The president approved top military appointments on the PM's advice under Article 243. | Important for Chapter 8B because it shows Sharif's formal role in a major civil-military decision. | Formal process only; it does not capture the informal balance of power behind the appointment. |

**Compact event map**
- April 9-11, 2022: Imran Khan is removed in a no-confidence vote; Shehbaz Sharif becomes PM and takes the oath of office.
- April 19, 2022: A 33-member coalition cabinet is sworn in.
- June 8, 2022: Energy shortages force a five-day workweek and broader conservation measures.
- July-August 2022: Inflation, reserve pressure, and currency stress intensify.
- August 6-19, 2022: Flood relief fund, cash relief, and emergency response become central government business.
- September-October 2022: UN and World Bank documents quantify the flood catastrophe and reconstruction burden.
- November 24-29, 2022: Sharif advises the top military appointments; Asim Munir takes command.

**Chapter source plan**
- `1B`: No strong cross-chapter narrative source retained here; if you later need ruler-specific nuclear/defense evidence, use dedicated official defense sources plus SIPRI/NTI-style independent references.
- `2B`: Mostly the supplied local priors; if you need narrative context, use the Reuters transition and energy-crisis pieces only as background, not as direct conflict attribution.
- `3B`: Best sources are Amnesty, Reuters on the transition, and the Urdu Radio Pakistan flood-response item for state response context.
- `4B`: Best sources are the constitution, Reuters transition reporting, APP oath/cabinet sources, and Amnesty for dissent constraints.
- `5B`: Best sources are Reuters inflation, IMF, and the World Bank PDNA for macro and welfare pressure.
- `6B`: Best sources are the Urdu Radio Pakistan relief fund item, UN flood response plan, and World Bank PDNA.
- `7B`: Best sources are IMF, Reuters inflation, and the World Bank PDNA for institutional stress and corruption-adjacent context.
- `8B`: Best sources are the constitution, IMF coalition-fragility language, APP cabinet formation, and the President's military-appointment notice.
